fix: The flora says this of the lamina, so leaf lamina (PO_0020039) would be the closer bearer, but 'leaf' is not false.
reason: 'lamina ... ± conduplicate' means the blade is folded lengthwise. Conduplicate with 'approximately' says exactly that.
The capsule (a fruit) is '± fleshy'. Fruit + fleshy + approximately says the same.
In Geranium the style-column is the fused styles. Length 5-7 mm with the stage set to mature matches 'at maturity'.

fix: 'Sterile leaves' are the leaves of the sterile shoots. A state slot for this would be more exact.
reason: The leaves are longer than the culm, and the comparison target is the culm, as the flora says.

fix: 'Branched' after a list of veins ('lateral veins ... the basal pair ...') belongs to the leaf veins (leaf lamina vein, PO_0020138), not to the general class vascular bundle.
reason: The branched part is the basal pair of lateral veins of the leaf blade.
'Lip rhombic-ovate': a shape between rhombic and ovate, recorded on the lip. The petals have the same shape, so either reading of the statement is true.
'Abaxially ... glabrescent' puts glabrescent on the underside of the blade. The bearer was replaced by the abaxial epidermis correctly.
'Stems ... not articulate' means the stem is not jointed. The negation covers only the jointed value.

fix: Position words before the organ ('Lower leaves', 'proximal cauline', 'distal ones') must fill the position slot. Without it, the trait is claimed for all leaves.
reason: The flora says this only of the lower leaves. The elliptic-to-lanceolate reading of 'elliptic-lanceolate' is right.

fix: A colour phrase like 'light green' must give the colour value (PATO_0001250 light green), not just the general quality 'color'.
reason: The stems are light green, but the annotation gives only 'color' with no value.
Liparis leaves narrowed to a sheathing base 'but not articulated': the leaf has no joint. The negation is scoped right.
'Fruit capsular' means the fruit is a capsule. Recording 'capsule fruit present' follows the reviewed rule.
These are the auricles of the leaf sheath (the text is about leaves, not the culm sheath), and they are absent.
'Thorns & Spines: Absent' makes thorns absent. Spines would be a second annotation.
The blade's abaxial surface is glabrous.
'(not cespitose)' is said of the whole plant. The negation covers only caespitose.
'Adaxially glandular hairy but glabrescent': the upper surface becomes glabrous.
The capsule is shorter than the calyx. Fruit, decreased length and the calyx as target all match.

fix: For whole plants, FNA writes 'a × b dm' as height × width. The first range is height and the second is width. Width here should be 1-2 dm = 10-20 cm, and 0.5-0.9 dm (5-9 cm) is the height.
reason: The annotation gives the height numbers (5-9 cm) as the plant's width.

fix: 'Proximal cauline' must fill the position slot (lower stem leaves). Without it, 'leaves ± petiolate' is claimed for all leaves.
reason: Only the lower stem leaves are subpetiolate. 'Subpetiolate' read as approximately petiolate is acceptable.

fix: Strictly, only the pistillate panicles are said to be sparsely leafy. A state slot for 'pistillate' would be more exact.
reason: The panicles bear leaves, so inflorescence + leafy holds.
The leaf blade margin is entire.

fix: 'Outside' means the outer (abaxial) surface, and the standard petal would be a closer bearer. The plain reading on the petal is still true.
reason: The standard (a petal) is hairy on the outside.

fix: In 'adnate to the base of the X', X is the part fused to. 'Base of' is only the place on it. The target should be the corolla tube (or the corolla), not a general 'base'.
reason: The stamens are fused to the corolla tube near its base, but the target is a bare 'base' with no organ.
The blade thickness runs from thin to thick, as the flora says. 'Fleshy' would be a separate annotation.

fix: Where the flora splits leaves into 'major' and 'minor', the leaf kind must be kept. A trait of the minor leaf blade must not go on all leaf blades.
reason: The minor leaf has an obtuse apex, but the major leaf's apex is acute. Without this context the statement is partly false.

fix: Words after 'lateral lobes' describe the lobes (leaf lamina lobe, PO_0025517), not the whole blade.
reason: The lateral lobes are 'undivided or obliquely cuneate'. The blade itself is lobed, so 'blade undivided' is false.
The leaf blade margin is narrowly revolute.
The seeds are subspheric.

fix: In 'proximal ones leaflike, distal ones ...', the position must fill the position slot. Also, 'palmately cleft' fits the more specific palmatifid (FLOPO_0991351).
reason: Only the upper bracts are usually palmately cleft. The lower bracts are leaflike, so a claim about all bracts is wrong.
